rows.speaker: الطحاوي وغيره
rows.claim: They explain the stepdaughters' association with the household as describing the usual case; stepdaughters remain forbidden even when they are not actually in the man's custody.
rows.anchor: إضافتهن إلى الحجور حملا على أغلب ما يكون الربائب، وهي محرمة وإن لم تكن في الحجر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes “in your households” as explaining the prohibition: the girls are or may be raised by you, and after intercourse with their mothers they function like your own daughters.
rows.anchor: فائدته التعليل للتحريم، وأنهن لاحتضانكم لهن، أو لكونهن بصدد احتضانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from your wives who you have entered” appears to modify only the stepdaughters clause.
rows.anchor: من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن ظاهر هذا أنه متعلق بقوله: وربائبكم فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun modifies the wives governed by من, not the wives in “mothers of your wives,” because the two phrases have different grammatical governors.
rows.anchor: واللاتي: صفة لنسائكم المجرور بمن، ولا جائز أن يكون اللاتي وصفا لنسائكم من قوله: وأمهات نسائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase cannot be attached to an omitted element governing both mothers-in-law and stepdaughters: من identifies which wives for the former but marks origin for the latter.
rows.anchor: لاختلاف مدلول حرف الجر إذ ذاك، لأنه بالنسبة إلى قوله: وأمهات نسائكم يكون من نسائكم لبيان النساء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes attaching من نسائكم to both wives and stepdaughters, taking من to mean connection, as in the verse and cited expressions.
rows.anchor: إلا أن أعلقه بالنساء والربائب، وأجعل من للاتصال كقوله تعالى: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says no one recognizes “connection” as a meaning of من; the cited verse, poetry, and report have other explanations, and the proposed attachment makes the mothers-in-law phrase redundant and unidiomatic.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم أحدا ذهب إلى أن من معاني من الاتصال. وأما ما شبه به من الآية والشعر والحديث، فمتأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering upon a woman is a euphemism for intercourse, as in expressions meaning that a man built over her or put a veil over her.
rows.anchor: والدخول هنا كناية عن الجماع لقولهم: بنى عليها، وضرب عليها الحجاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس وابن دينار
rows.claim: They take the bāʾ as causative, meaning the women brought under the covering; on this view a man divorced after the wedding but before intercourse may marry her daughter.
rows.anchor: والباء: للتعدية، والمعنى: اللاتي أدخلتموهن الستر قاله: ابن عباس، وطاوس، وابن دينار

rows.speaker: عطاء ومالك وأبو حنيفة والثوري والأوزاعي والليث والشافعي
rows.claim: These jurists, in one of al-Shafiʿi's positions, hold that touching the woman with desire makes both her mother and daughter forbidden, as well as making her forbidden to the man's father and son.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء، ومالك، وأبو حنيفة، والثوري، والأوزاعي، والليث: إذا مسها بشهوة حرمت عليه أمها وابنتها

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى والشافعي ومالك والكوفيون
rows.claim: On lustful looking, Ibn Abi Layla and al-Shafiʿi require touching; Malik counts looking pleasurably at hair or beauty; the Kufans count lustful looking at the genital area.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في النظر إليها بشهوة، فقال ابن أبي ليلى: لا يحرم النظر حتى تلمس، وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri says looking at her genital area is prohibitive when deliberate, without stipulating desire.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري: يحرم إذا كان تعمد النظر إلى فرجها، ولم يذكر الشهوة

rows.speaker: عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان
rows.claim: They say looking at a woman's genital area bars marriage to her mother or daughter, and extend this ruling to enslaved women.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء، وحماد بن أبي سليمان: إذا نظر إلى فرج امرأة فلا ينكح أمها ولا ابنتها، وعدوا هذا الحكم إلى الإماء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says an enslaved woman is never lawful for the owner's son if he has touched her lustfully, uncovered her, or kissed her.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: إذا ملك الأمة وغمزها بشهوة، أو كشفها، أو قبلها، لا تحل لولده بحال

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq ordered that his enslaved woman be sold after his death, saying even his limited touching and looking had made her forbidden to his son.
rows.anchor: وأمر مسروق أن تباع جاريته بعد موته وقال: أما إني لم أصب منها إلا ما يحرمها على ولدي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar stripped an enslaved woman with whom he had been alone; when his son asked for her, Umar said she was not lawful to him.
rows.anchor: وجرد عمر أمة خلا بها فاستوهبها ابن له فقال: لا تحل لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No blame if you did not enter upon them” means no blame in marrying the stepdaughters, but permission also presupposes separation from their mothers by divorce or the mothers' death.
rows.anchor: وليس جواز نكاح الربائب موقوفا على انتفاء مطلق الدخول، بل لا بد من محذوف مقدر تقديره: فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن، وفارقتموهن بطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jurists agree that a father's contracted wife is forbidden to his son and a son's contracted wife to his father, whether intercourse occurred; حليلة means wife rather than an enslaved concubine, so the contract itself suffices.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على تحريم ما عقد عليه الآباء على الأبناء، وما عقد عليه الأبناء على الآباء كان مع العقد وطء، أو لم يكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From your loins” limits sons to biological sons and removes the metaphorical sense used for adopted sons; the verse about Muhammad not being the father of any of their men addresses that usage.
rows.anchor: وجاء الذين من أصلابكم وهو وصف لقوله: أبنائكم، برفع المجاز الذي يحتمله لفظ أبنائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet married Zaynab bint Jahsh after Zayd ibn Harithah divorced her, and jurists agree a foster son's wife is forbidden just like a biological son's wife.
rows.anchor: وقد تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الأسدية وهي بنت عمته، أميمة بنت عبد المطلب حين فارقها زيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root شجر denotes confusion or entanglement; it also means disputing, and its uses for howdah braces, a branching spear, and intertwined affection illustrate the root's interlacing sense.
rows.anchor: شجر الأمر: التبس، يشجر شجورا وشجرا، وشاجر الرجل غيره في الأمر نازعه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نفَر describes a man setting out urgently; the root originally conveys alarm, and going to someone means seeking relief from fear. النفير can mean a group, while a fleeing animal hurries away.
rows.anchor: نفر الرجل ينفر نفيرا، خرج مجدا بكسر الفاء في المضارع وضمها، وأصله الفزع

rows.speaker: الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi defines ثبة as a group of two or three in Arab usage; another view says it is a group of more than ten men.
rows.anchor: الثبة: الجماعة الاثنان والثلاثة في كلام العرب قاله: الماتريدي. وقيل: هي فوق العشرة من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He discusses ثبة's pattern and disputed final letter, deriving it either from praising a man by assembling his merits or from ثبا يثبو; its plurals and the basin's central pool have related forms.
rows.anchor: وزنها فعلة. ولامها قيل: واو، وقيل: ياء، مشتقة من تثبيت على الرجل إذا أثنيت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the basin's ثبة as its middle, where water gathers, and derives it from ثاب يثوب; البطء means holding back from something.
rows.anchor: وثبة الحوض وسطه الذي يثوب الماء إليه، المحذوف منه عينه، لأنه من ثاب يثوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: They understand تسليم as yielding and submitting to the Prophet's judgment without objection.
rows.anchor: ويسلموا أي ينقادوا ويذعنوا لقضائك، لا يعارضون فيه بشيء قاله: ابن عباس والجمهور

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi gives another sense: they should hand over their dispute for the Prophet's judgment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ويسلموا ما تنازعوا فيه لحكمك، ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun تسليما emphasizes that submission truly occurs, and its placement is apt as a verse ending.
rows.anchor: وأكد الفعل بالمصدر على سبيل صدور التسليم حقيقة، وحسنه كونه فاصلة

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads شجر with a silent jīm, apparently to avoid successive vowel movements; Abu Hayyan finds this weak because fatḥa is light, unlike damma and kasra, whose replacement with sukūn is established in Tamim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال: فيما شجر بسكون الجيم، وكأنه فر من توالي الحركات، وليس بقوي لخفة الفتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion was a Jewish taunt that hypocrites rejected the Messenger's judgment despite Jews obeying a command to kill themselves: they claimed seventy thousand had been killed. Thabit ibn Qays replied that Muslims would obey, and the verse came down.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود لما لم يرض المنافق بحكم الرسول: ما رأينا أسخف من هؤلاء يؤمنون بمحمد ويتبعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical command means killing oneself by one's own hand or one another, or leaving home as prescribed for Israelites after the calf; only a few would obey, a severe rebuke.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أنه تعالى لو فرض عليهم أن يقتلوا أنفسهم، إما أن يقتل نفسه بيده، أو يقتل بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: السبيعي
rows.claim: Al-Subayʿi reports that after the verse a man said they would obey if commanded and thanked God for sparing them; the Prophet replied that some in his community have faith firmer than lofty mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال السبيعي: لما نزلت قال رجل: لو أمرنا لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي عافانا

rows.speaker: ابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb identifies the man who made that remark as Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن وهب: الرجل القائل ذلك هو أبو بكر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: A further report quotes Abu Bakr saying that if the command had been written for them, he would have begun with himself and his family.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قال: لو كتب علينا ذلك لبدأت بنفسي وأهل بيتي

rows.speaker: النقاش وأبو الليث السمرقندي
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash names Umar as the speaker; Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi instead names Ammar, Ibn Masud, and Thabit ibn Qays.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقاش: أنه عمر. وذكر أبو الليث السمرقندي: أن القائل منهم عمار، وابن مسعود، وثابت بن قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes “upon them” to mean the hypocrites alone: a few would comply ostentatiously, exposing their unbelief when the command became difficult.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليهم قيل: يعود على المنافقين، أي: ما فعله إلا قليل منهم رياء وسمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “upon them” to include all people, believers and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعود على الناس مؤمنهم ومنافقهم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وعاصم وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads the nūn of أن with kasra and the wāw of أو with ḍamma; Hamza and Asim read both with kasra, while the other canonical readers use ḍamma for both.
rows.anchor: وكسر النون من أن، وضم الواو من أو، أبو عمرو. وكسرهما حمزة وعاصم، وضمهما باقي السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن can be explanatory or a verbal-noun particle, given the stated rule that it can introduce an imperative verb.
rows.anchor: وأن هنا يحتمل أن تكون تفسيرية، وأن تكون مصدرية على ما قرروا أن أن توصل بفعل الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of leaving homes with killing selves shows how difficult emigration is; the Companions nevertheless left their homes and families when God commanded them to migrate.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على صعوبة الخروج من الديار، إذ قرنه الله تعالى بقتل الأنفس، وقد خرج الصحابة المهاجرون من ديارهم وفارقوا أهاليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reads قليل nominative, as a substitute for the wāw in فعلوه according to Basrans or coordinated with the pronoun according to Kufans; the usual rule is to match what follows إلا to what precedes it.
rows.anchor: وبالرفع قرأ الجمهور. وقرأ أبي، وابن أبي إسحاق، وابن عامر، وعيسى بن عمر: إلا قليلا بالنصب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the accusative reading as a normal exception or as an omitted فعلًا after إلا; Abu Hayyan accepts the first account but rejects the second as weak and inconsistent with the nominative sense and the phrase منهم.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقرىء إلا قليلا بالنصب على أصل الاستثناء، أو على إلا فعلا قليلا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the object pronoun in فعلوه refers to both killing and leaving, since the action is one genus in different forms; Abu Hayyan calls this explanation non-grammatical.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: الكناية في قوله ما فعلوه عائد على القتل والخروج معا، وذلك لأن الفعل جنس واحد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says what they are admonished to do is follow, obey, and submit to the Prophet's judgments, which benefits both lives and strengthens faith against instability.
rows.anchor: ما يوعظون به من اتباع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وطاعته، والانقياد لما يراه ويحكم به

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes the verse to mean that these hypocrites should accept admonition and repent, with تثبيتا meaning certainty and affirmation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ولو أن هؤلاء المنافقين اتعظوا وأنابوا لكان خيرا لهم وتثبيتا معناه يقينا وتصديقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says both explanations depart from the apparent wording: what they are admonished by is not simply obedience or repentance, and the text does not say “what they are commanded.”
rows.anchor: وكلاهما شرح ما يوعظون به بخلاف ما يدل عليه الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes admonition to mean command: they should do what they are ordered and stop what they are forbidden to do.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الوعظ هنا بمعنى الأمر أي: ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يؤمرون به فانتهوا عما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: ري الظمآن
rows.claim: Rī al-Ẓamʾān explains the phrase as what they are advised and commanded to do, namely sincerity and submission.
rows.anchor: وقال في ري الظمآن: ما يوعظون به أي: ما يوصون ويؤمرون به من الإخلاص والتسليم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says the verse reports that accepting admonition would be better for them.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: أخبر أنهم لو قبلوا الموعظة لكان خيرا لهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi takes it as doing what they are charged and commanded to do; obligations are called admonition because they come with promises, threats, encouragement, warnings, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: المراد أنهم لو فعلوا ما كلفوا به وأمروا، وسمي هذا التكليف والأمر وعظا

rows.speaker: الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi reports the explanation that what they are admonished to do is the command of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال الماتريدي: وقيل ما يوعظون به من الأمر من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the apparent sense: admonition is a reminder of the punishment for disobeying God, so the object is what warns them; read the bāʾ as causal and supply “leaving it,” yielding the thing they are admonished because of leaving undone.
rows.anchor: لأن الوعظ هو التذكار بما يحل بمن خالف أمر الله تعالى من العقاب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the good may be the good of both worlds, rather than a comparative; alternatively, it means more beneficial, while obedience gives stronger confirmation because truth lasts, obedience leads to more obedience, and people seek to preserve acquired good.
rows.anchor: لكان خيرا لهم: أي يحصل لهم خير الدارين، فلا يكون أفعل التفضيل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi connects “better for them” to first obtaining good and “more confirming” to its continued preservation.
rows.anchor: فقوله: لكان خيرا لهم إشارة إلى الحالة الأولى. وقوله: وأشد تثبيتا إشارة إلى الحالة الثانية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats إذا as answering an implicit question about what further benefit follows confirmation: if they were steadfast, God would give them reward.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وإذا جواب لسؤال مقدر كأنه قيل: وماذا يكون لهم أيضا بعد التثبيت؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the implication that إذا always serves jointly as answer and condition: al-Farisi distinguishes answer-only uses from answer-and-condition uses, while Abu Ali says it is always both; Abu Hayyan prefers al-Farisi as the sound grammatical account.
rows.anchor: والصحيح قول الفارسي، وهي مسألة يبحث عنها في علم النحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward is a metonym for recompense for obedience; its greatness refers either to abundance or to nobility.
rows.anchor: والأجر كناية عن الثواب على الطاعة، ووصفه بالعظم باعتبار الكثرة، أو باعتبار الشرف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets the straight path as faith leading to Paradise; other reported explanations are the road to Paradise or righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم هو الإيمان المؤدي إلى الجنة قاله: ابن عطية. وقيل: هو الطريق إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Because guidance to faith precedes reward, Ibn Atiyya says the verse lists blessings rather than their chronological order and means God guided them beforehand to qualify for reward; if the path means Paradise's road or good deeds, the sequence is chronological.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن الهداية قبل إعطاء الأجر، لأن المقصد إنما هو تعديد ما كان الله ينعم به عليهم دون ترتيب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Thawban, who loved the Prophet deeply and feared that his lower rank in Paradise would keep him from seeing the Prophet in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان شديد الحب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن زيد بن عبد ربه الأنصاري
rows.claim: A similar account is told of Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih, the man shown the call to prayer: he feared that after death the Prophet would be in the highest realm and they would not see or meet him, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وحكي مثل قول ثوبان عن جماعة من الصحابة منهم: عبد الله بن زيد بن عبد ربه الأنصاري، وهو الذي أري الأذان

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki reports that Abd Allah prayed after the Prophet's death to be blinded so he would see nothing after him, and became blind.
rows.anchor: وحكى مكي عن عبد الله هذا أنه لما مات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: اللهم أعمني حتى لا أرى شيئا بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being “with” the favored means sharing one abode, where each person is content with his place and can see the others despite distance.
rows.anchor: والمعنى في مع النبيين: إنه معهم في دار واحدة، وكل من فيها رزق الرضا بحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the believers may be raised to the prophets' stations when they wish as an honor, then return to their own stations.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعية هنا كونهم يرفعون إلى منازل الأنبياء متى شاؤوا تكرمة لهم، ثم يعودون إلى منازلهم

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the prophets, truthful ones, and martyrs descend to those below them to recall God's blessing together.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الأنبياء والصديقين والشهداء ينحدرون إلى من أسفل منهم ليتذاكروا نعمة الله، ذكره المهدوي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi interprets the afterlife as illuminating souls with knowledge and joining them with prophets: perfected spirits retain worldly ties with complete spirits after separation, reflecting their light and strengthening it; this is not equality of rank.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله الرازي: هذه الآية تنبيه على أمرين من أحوال المعاد: الأول: إشراق الأرواح بأنوار المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says al-Razi's account resembles philosophers' doctrine of disembodied souls, whose language and meanings Muslims reject; affection for a doctrine can make it appear in one's speech.
rows.anchor: وهو شبيه بما قالته الفلاسفة في الأرواح إذا فارقت الأجساد. وأهل الإسلام يأبون هذه الألفاظ ومدلولاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With those God favored” explains the straight path of those favored; “from the prophets” explains the favored people, so obedient believers are joined to the earlier favored ones.
rows.anchor: وقوله: مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم، تفسير لقوله: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم وهم من ذكر في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says the four groups correspond by rank and reward: prophet with prophet, truthful one with truthful one, martyr with martyr, and righteous person with righteous person.
rows.anchor: ممن أنعم عليهم من الفرق الأربع في المنزلة والثواب: النبي بالنبي، والصديق بالصديق، والشهيد بالشهيد، والصالح بالصالح

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib alternatively attaches “from the prophets” to “whoever obeys,” making it refer to prophets and those after them, while “with those favored” refers to the highest assembly; he cites the Prophet's deathbed prayer for the highest companion.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الراغب أن يتعلق من النبيين بقوله: ومن يطع الله والرسول. أي: من النبيين ومن بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects that reading in meaning and grammar: it would imply prophets during or after Muhammad obey him, impossible because he is the seal of prophets and said no prophet follows him; moreover, what precedes the result fāʾ cannot govern after it.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الذي هو عنده ظاهر فاسد من جهة المعنى، ومن جهة النحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ whether truthful, martyrs, and righteous are overlapping descriptions of one person or three distinct classes.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في الأوصاف الثلاثة التي بعد النبيين. فقال بعضهم: كلها أوصاف لموصوف واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form meaning either one who tells much truth or one who gives much charity.
rows.anchor: فأما الصديق فهو فعيل للمبالغة كشريب. فقيل: هو الكثير الصدق، وقيل: هو الكثير الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation calls everyone who believes without any doubt a truthful one, citing the verse that those who believe in God and His messengers are the truthful.
rows.anchor: أن كل من صدق بكل الذي لا يتخالجه فيه شك فهو صديق لقوله تعالى: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the truthful as the foremost Companions or the first person to affirm the Messenger, becoming a model for others.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أفاضل أصحاب الرسول. الثالث: السابق إلى تصديق الرسول. فصار في ذلك قدوة لسائر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common explanation of martyr is one killed in God's path, specially honored in death; legal rules distinguish them from others in washing and prayer, and the verse's term includes the kinds of martyrs mentioned by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأما الشهيد: فهو المقتول في سبيل الله، المخصوص بفضل الميتة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects limiting martyrdom to being killed by an unbeliever; he derives شهيد as an active participle for one who bears witness to God's religion by argument and explanation or by sword and spear.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: لا يجوز أن تكون الشهادة مفسرة بكون الإنسان مقتول الكافر، بل نقول: الشهيد فعيل بمعنى فاعل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi identifies martyrs as those who uphold justice and links them to the verse “God bears witness that there is no god but He.”
rows.anchor: فالشهداء هم القائمون بالقسط، وهم الذين ذكرهم الله في قوله: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous person is one whose belief and deeds are sound.
rows.anchor: والصالح: هو الذي يكون صالحا في اعتقاده وعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If these are separate classes, their order descends from highest to lower; the promise encourages believers to obey God and His Messenger by offering companionship with God's nearest and highest servants.
rows.anchor: وجاء هذا التركيب على هذا القول على حسب التنزل من الأعلى إلى الأدنى، إلى أدنى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers this grammatical parsing as more eloquent: the alternative requires an implicit subject before lā, since a present verb negated by lā cannot take the circumstantial wāw.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه عندي أعرب وأفصح، لأن الأول يحتاج إلى إضمار مبتدأ، قبل لا، حتى تكون الجملة اسمية في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads the verb without the emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: ليبينونه بغير نون التوكيد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the emphatic nūn need not follow the emphatic lām, attributing this allowance to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقد لا تلزم هذه النون لام التوكيد، قاله: سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Basrans know the lām and nūn only alternating by poetic necessity, while Kufans allow it in ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس معروفا من قول البصريين، بل تعاقب اللام والنون عندهم ضرورة. والكوفيون يجيزون ذلك في سعة الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites an anonymous poetic line using the lām construction as evidence for the permissive usage.
rows.anchor: وعيشك يا سلمى لأوقن إنني ... لما شئت مستحل ولو أنه القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous poetic line likewise uses the construction to support the permissive usage.
rows.anchor: يمينا لأبغض كل امرئ ... يزخرف قولا ولا يفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the covenant as taken from the prophets, with the command that they make it clear to people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: ميثاق النبيين لتبيننه للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Abbas's reading, the pronoun in “they cast it away” refers to the people, since it cannot refer to the prophets; the people discarded the covenant explained to them.
rows.anchor: فيعود الضمير في فنبذوه على الناس إذ يستحيل عوده على النبيين، أي: فنبذه الناس المبين لهم الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the phrase about casting behind their backs to the earlier account of a party among the People of the Book discarding God's Book.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير معنى: فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم في قوله: نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن زيد وجماعة
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about hypocrites who stayed behind on campaigns, made excuses on return, and received the Prophet's apparent acceptance and prayer for forgiveness, thereby being exposed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في المنافقين كانوا يتخلفون عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الغزو، فإذا جاء استعذروا له

rows.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many commentators instead identify the people addressed as Jewish rabbis.
rows.anchor: وقال كثير من المفسرين: نزلت في أحبار اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains أتوا as “did”; the parallel reading of Ubayy has فعلوا, and the same sense appears in 19:61, where مأتيا means مفعولا.
rows.anchor: وأتى تكون بمعنى فعل، كقوله تعالى: إنه كان وعده مأتيا أي مفعولا. فمعنى بما أتوا بما فعلوا، ويدل عليه قراءة أبي بما فعلوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One Ibn Abbas explanation is that they concealed what the Messenger asked and gave him a different answer, then sought his praise for supposedly informing him.
rows.anchor: أحدها كتم ما سألهم عنه الرسول، وإخبارهم بغيره، وأروه أنهم قد أخبروه به واستحمدوا بذلك إليه قاله: ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas explanation is that they rejoiced in worldly gains and wanted to be praised as scholars.
rows.anchor: الثاني ما أصابوا من الدنيا وأحبوا أن يقال: إنهم علماء قاله: ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says they claimed to follow Abraham's religion while concealing the Messenger's matter.
rows.anchor: الثالث قولهم: نحن على دين إبراهيم، وكتمهم أمر الرسول قاله: ابن جبير

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say they wrote Jews everywhere that Muhammad was no prophet and urged them to remain in their religion, while claiming to be devoted worshippers and God's allies.
rows.anchor: الرابع كتبهم إلى اليهود يهود الأرض كلها أن محمدا ليس بنبي، فاثبتوا على دينكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies Jews of Khaybar who professed support and adherence to the Prophet's religion while persisting in error and seeking praise they had not earned.
rows.anchor: الخامس قول يهود خيبر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه: نحن على دينكم، ونحن لكم ردء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reported explanation is that Jews equipped and financed an army against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: السادس تجهيز اليهود جيشا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإنفاقهم على ذلك الجيش
